summary: Candidate A is closer to the frozen contract because it preserves FilesService.Add and explicitly validates Upload inputs. Candidate B materially changes Add’s behavior and still does not route Upload through the public Add method.
reasons: A preserves the existing Add implementation, while B unconditionally reads and buffers every caller-built Add body, changing streaming, memory use, error wrapping, and when reader errors occur.
A explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before body construction; B has no visible Upload validation for either condition.
Both reuse internal/multipartbody.NewFile and produce a replayable Upload body.

Neither follows the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add: A duplicates Add’s request/response logic, while B introduces a private add method and has both public methods call that instead. A’s defect is easier to correct with a direct return s.Add(...). B would additionally need its Add behavior restored and validation added explicitly inside Upload before calling Add.
risks_a: Upload duplicates option handling, Raw.Do invocation, response decoding, and missing-data handling instead of delegating to Add, creating divergence risk.
Tests do not cover source-reader errors.
The retry test uses bytes.NewReader as the source rather than a streamed source such as os.File, so streamed-content coverage is less direct.
risks_b: Add no longer preserves existing behavior because it buffers all custom multipart bodies in memory and wraps source errors with new text.
Upload lacks explicit empty-filename and nil-content validation.

Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, contrary to the required delegation path, even though request handling is shared privately afterward intentionally anyway; as written it fails the literal public API routing contract intent especially around preserving Add semantics centrally without replacing them with a new layer machinery duplication concern remains minor compared to behavior change in Add itself; tests also remove the prior straightforward Add test instead of retaining it alongside retry coverage, weakening direct regression coverage of its original behavior and source-reader errors are untested.
